macro.label: risk-off tilt

drivers.label: Brent
drivers.india: India imports about 88% of the crude it burns and pays for it in dollars. Roughly $10/bbl is 0.3-0.4pp on headline CPI and around $14bn on the current account, which is why this channel reaches the rate path and not only the oil names.

drivers.label: Crude WTI
drivers.india: The same channel as Brent and largely the same information. Weighted low on purpose: India prices its basket off Brent and Dubai, so counting WTI at full weight would double-count one move.

drivers.label: Dollar index
drivers.india: The one driver that splits the index. A bid dollar pulls FPI money out of cash equity, which is negative for NIFTY -- and is simultaneously positive for the exporters inside it, because IT and pharma bill in dollars and pay costs in rupees. Read the index effect and the sector effect as two separate facts, not as a contradiction.

drivers.label: USD/INR
drivers.india: The rupee itself, which does not always follow the dollar index -- RBI intervention and importer demand move it on their own. Weighted below the dollar index because the two overlap, and kept separate because when they disagree the disagreement is the signal.

drivers.label: US 10-year
drivers.india: The discount rate on long-duration India. It compresses the multiple the market will pay before it touches a single earnings estimate, which is why it hits the expensive end of the market hardest. Note ref is 2% OF THE YIELD, so about 10bp on a 5% handle -- not 2 percentage points.

drivers.label: VIX
drivers.india: Global risk appetite in one number. It is not an India channel in itself -- it is the channel through which every other risk asset gets sold at once, and India VIX follows it with a lag more often than it leads.

drivers.label: Copper
drivers.india: Realisation for the integrated producers, and the standing proxy for global industrial demand. Reaches NIFTY METAL properly and the broad index only faintly -- it is four large stocks, not the market.

drivers.label: Iron ore 62%
drivers.india: Steel realisation against input cost. Positive for the integrated miners and negative for the converters, so the index effect is smaller than the sector noise suggests.

drivers.label: Gold
drivers.india: Read here as a risk-off confirmation rather than as a commodity: when gold is bid alongside the dollar, the tape is hedging rather than rotating. It is also a live import-bill line, and the gold-loan books mark against it.

drivers.label: Nat Gas
drivers.india: City-gas input cost. The pass-through is regulated and lagged, so a move lands on margin well before it lands on the consumer.

drivers.label: Soybean oil
drivers.india: Standing in for crude palm oil, India's largest edible-oil import, which has no free feed. Moves FMCG gross margin within a quarter and shows up in food CPI before that.

drivers.label: Wheat
drivers.india: Food is roughly 46% of the CPI basket. A sustained move here is the fastest route there is from a commodity screen to a rate decision.

drivers.label: Sugar #11
drivers.india: Sector-local rather than index-level, and policy dominates it: the export quota decides the domestic price far more than the world price does.

drivers.label: Coal API2
drivers.india: Imported thermal coal, which sets the marginal cost of power and the input cost of every converter. Small weight because most Indian generation burns domestic coal at a regulated price.

macro.verdict: Global bias -31, risk-off tilt. Heaviest drag: US 10-year +2.10% (-13). Largest offset: Nat Gas -2.07% (+2). The stance is unchanged by this: it is context for the size of a gap, not a view on its direction.

events.label: India WPI
events.note: The input-cost read. Confirms or contradicts what the crude and metal channels have been saying.

events.label: India trade data
events.note: Merchandise trade balance. The direct read on what the oil bill and a weak rupee are actually costing.

events.label: China activity data
events.note: Industrial production, retail sales and fixed-asset investment together. Fixed-asset investment is the construction read, and construction is what iron ore and copper are actually a bet on.

events.label: US retail sales
events.note: Consumer demand. Matters here only when it is far enough from expectation to move the rate path.

events.label: PBoC loan prime rate
events.note: The policy rate. Moves the yuan, and the yuan is the currency the metal complex takes its cue from when the dollar is quiet.

events.label: China NBS PMI
events.note: Sets the tone for the entire metal channel at once -- copper, aluminium and iron ore all price off Chinese industrial demand. Published on the last day of the month whatever day that falls on, so it often lands on a weekend and is priced at the next open.

events.label: US ISM Manufacturing
events.note: The global growth proxy the dollar trades off. Also the cleanest read on whether the copper move is demand or positioning.

events.label: China Caixin Manufacturing PMI
events.note: The private survey, weighted to smaller and more export-facing firms. When it disagrees with the NBS print, the disagreement is the signal.

events.label: GST collections
events.note: Monthly indirect-tax take. A growth read the market treats as confirmation rather than news.

events.label: India Manufacturing PMI
events.note: Survey data -- moves the narrative more than the index.

events.label: India Services PMI
events.note: Services is the larger share of the economy and the smaller share of the market's attention.

events.label: US ISM Services
events.note: The larger half of the US economy and the smaller half of the dollar's reaction to it.

events.label: RBI MPC decision
events.note: Repo rate decision ends the Dec 2-4 meeting; moves bank stocks, the rupee and short-end yields. Source: RBI press release prid=62422.
events.providers: Reserve Bank of India, Your calendar

events.label: US nonfarm payrolls
events.note: The largest scheduled mover of the dollar and the 10-year there is, and it moves both in the same print. Two live channels on this desk repriced at 18:00 IST, after the Indian close.

events.label: China trade data
events.note: Import volumes for crude and for copper: the demand side of two of this desk's channels in a single release.

events.label: FOMC decision
events.note: Fed rate decision 2:00 PM ET (after Indian close); sets the dollar and US 10-year that drive FII flows. Source: Fed 2026 calendar.

events.label: China CPI and PPI
events.note: PPI is the one that matters here. Chinese factory-gate deflation is exported straight into the metal complex.

side.why: Implied is only 1.00x the forecast, below the 1.10x a seller needs. A reason to buy is present (realised vol rising above implied) but buying on it has not paid on this desk's history.
